subject: Clarifying no-train scope, prompt/response IP, and subprocessor transfer plan
messages:
From: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@healthops.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA follow-up — no-train scope and transfer options

Hi Elliot,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal has one more set of clarifying questions before we proceed with the procurement checklist:

1) No-train / model improvement: we need a clear commitment that any data we send via the API under our production account will not be used to train or improve models (including derivative datasets). Is Redwood able to make a written no-train commitment scoped to our tenant?

2) Prompt and response IP: we require confirmation that customer prompts and model responses are not claimed as Redwood IP and that we retain rights to our prompts and outputs.

3) Subprocessors & transfers: please share the current subprocessor inventory and whether any subprocessors process data outside the US. If transfer is required, what mechanisms are used (SCCs, EU adequacy, etc.)?

4) Evidence: legal would like a short evidence pack (SOC2 summary + example audit log excerpt + SFTP export path or escrow plan) to attach to the contract.

Can you route to the right folks and give an ETA? We are aiming to sign the SOW by the end of next week.

Best,
Sofia
Head of Security & Compliance
HealthOps Inc.

From: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@healthops.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA follow-up — no-train scope and transfer options

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear list. Routing to legal and infra for specifics; summary below and we can attach docs/links.

Short answers (high level):
- No-train: Redwood offers an account-level no-training flag for paid production accounts; when enabled, data is excluded from model improvement pipelines and derivative datasets. We can put that in the DPA as a commitment scoped to the account and tenant IDs.
- Prompt/response IP: we do not claim ownership over customer prompts or outputs. Customers retain output rights; Redwood retains model & system improvements that do not expose customer content. We can provide contract language for that.
- Subprocessors & transfers: we maintain an inventory and support SCCs for EU transfers; some infra subprocessors operate in multi-region clouds. We can provide the CSV export and mark locations per subprocessor.
- Evidence: attaching SOC2 summary and sample audit log is fine. For data export/escrow we offer two options: SFTP nightly export (customer-provided endpoint) or escrow snapshot via signed transfer to an escrow partner.

Next steps: lauren (Legal) will propose DPA text for the no-train clause; dev (Infra) will export subprocessor inventory and confirm residency/transfer mechanisms. I will compile the evidence pack and propose wording for prompt/response ownership. ETA EOD 2027-09-02.

Thanks — Elliot
VP, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: elliot_price@redwood.com, sofia.martinez@healthops.com
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA follow-up — no-train scope and transfer options

Hi Sofia / team — looping in Marissa (Contracts) and Dev (Infra). Attaching a DPA excerpt and the proposed no-train clause language for initial review. Also including a short definition section to avoid ambiguity ("Customer Data", "Derived Models", "Model Improvements").

Key proposed contract points (draft):
- No-Train Commitment: "Redwood shall not use Customer Data to train, tune, or otherwise improve production or research models for any purpose beyond providing inference services to the subscribing Customer, subject to agreed exception list (e.g., aggregated telemetry for service reliability with no content retention)."
- Narrowed Derivative Rights: "Customer retains ownership of prompts and outputs. Redwood shall not claim ownership of generated outputs; any derivatives generated solely from Customer Data shall be governed by Customer's rights."
- Incident & Audit Evidence: Redwood will provide a SOC2 summary, recent penetration test report URL, and an example audit log extract (redacted) showing API request/response metadata.
- Subprocessor Transfers: Redwood will provide the full inventory CSV with location column. For transfers outside the EU, Redwood will rely on SCCs or equivalent documented transfer safeguards.

Attachments referenced: redwood-dpa-draft.pdf, subprocessor-inventory-2027-08.csv (see attached).

If HealthOps agrees in principle I can bake this into the SOW exhibit and share a tracked-change DPA by EOD.

- Lauren
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

[Attachment stubs: redwood-dpa-draft.pdf (application/pdf), subprocessor-inventory-2027-08.csv (text/csv)]

From: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@healthops.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA follow-up — no-train scope and transfer options

Hi all — thank you, that coverage looks good and the draft language addresses our core concerns. A few follow-ups:

- Can you confirm whether the no-train flag can be retroactive for data processed during the contract term (i.e., remove any training-derived weights or exclude past logs)? We understand full retroactive removal may be operationally limited; please outline what is feasible.
- For the SFTP nightly export option: what fields are included in the export (full responses, timestamps, request IDs)? We need enough to perform regression checks on our side.
- On subprocessors: please mark any subprocessors that have access to request/response payloads vs those that are operations-only. That distinction is important for our internal risk assessment.

If you can answer these by COB today we can get the DPA exhibit finalized and move to procurement. Appreciate the fast turn.

Best,
Sofia
